evidence: The public app is a no-sign-in JS/HTML editor, preview, console and saved-history library (frozen task/instruction.md:1-7; environment/instructions/overview.md:3-7; ui.md:3-9). No public instruction supplies file import/export/upload. Three dimension-prompt instances describe that unrelated file-transfer workflow: frozen task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:7 permits comparing 'imported/exported user files'; :102 includes 'upload' as an action; task/tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:43 refers to 'import' in its visual-credit guidance. The security note's dynamic module import is a different, valid restriction. The remaining prompts, shared app_context and parsed criterion descriptions align with the app's account-free workspace and saved snippets. Exact quotations, adversarial pair, and file hashes are in per-row-review/evidence/48/findings.md. No live judge run tested whether the wording changed scoring.
counterexample: A conforming Colderwater playground can type and run .js/.html code, Save/Load snippets, and inspect history with no import/export/upload control. Those three references can invite an off-task file-transfer probe, whereas a weak shell's upload button earns no requested playground behavior.
suggested_fix: Delete the imported/exported-user-files phrase and upload action example from Functional, and the import example from Visual; retain the dynamic import security probes that the public note requires.
